newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended near the day's weakest levels as a soft opening on Wall Street knocked already sliding stocks, distressed by the rand's fall to fresh six-month lows on the U.S. dollar, down further.

But music to retailing group CNA-Gallo was able to buck the trend jumping over nine percent to a new year high of 520 cents towards the close following the purchase of its retail business by clothing retailer Wooltru last week.

"The market is down on the U.S. Treasuries, expectations of a (local) rate cut which some people expected to be concluded before the weekend, the weaker rand and bonds," said Peer Ieul, managing director at UAL Securities.

U.S. Treasuries weakened on Friday night after the release of inflationary jobs data, sparking renewed fears of an interest rate hike there. On Monday Dow industrials opened some 50 points down as bond yields continued to rise.
In contrast South African markets have been discounting a rate cut, which has recently fuelled new record highs on the stock market.
But the rand's fall to a low of 4.6650 earlier, erased any hopes of gains on Monday although a few gold shares were supported as the randgold price benefitted.
Heavyweight gold stock Vaal Reefs advanced 400 cents to 239 rand, helping the all gold index up 6.3 points to 970.1.
The industrial index lost 35.3 points to 9,110.2, depressing the all-share index to end off 11.6 points at 7,445.2.
A handful of rand-hedge stocks also gained ground including minerals group Minorco which added 325 cents 95.25 rand.

Turnover was slow at around 528 million rand's worth compared with a daily average of around 750 million which dealers blamed on a dearth of economic data this week and the market's wait for an interest rate cut.
Listing of chemical stock Sentrachem was suspended pending a major announcement which turned out to be an offer by U.S. giant Dow Chemical for the group at 10.50 rand a share.
The market welcomed the news, saying it was a good price and would help make up for the firm's recent poor results.
"It is about time Sentrachem came out with some good news," Ieul said.
The Johannesburg Stock Exchange had by the close of trading not decided when to reinstate the stock.

But bank NRB Holdings jumped 25 percent to a new 1997 high of 775 on robust earnings prospects and following last week's clearing of a line of stock in the market, dealers said. Parent SMG Holdings followed suit, ending up 14 cents at 134 cents after earlier hitting a new year high of 136 cents..

Technology and manufacturing firms City Investment Holdings and Spicer-Mitchell fell after a profit warning at the weekend. Cityhold lost 13 percent to 26 cents and Spicer slid over six percent to 28 cents, recovering from an earlier 20 cent low.

Equity futures contracts mirrored movements in stocks with industrial contracts staying soft and gold contracts edging up. The September all-share contract was last at 6,670/77 from 6,711, the industrial contract at 8,599/607 from 8,666 and the near-month gold contract at 675/90 from 685.
